title: Aviadenovirus Coverage Audit
standfirst: Aviadenoviruses have the largest adenovirus genomes, about 44 kb, with dozens of lineage-specific ORFs at both ends. The core is called in essentially every near-complete genome; the open work is the avian ORFs the module does not yet declare.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Aviadenoviruses of poultry and wild birds, including fowl adenoviruses A–E with one or two fiber genes.

blocks.html: Fowl adenovirus 1 (Phelps) carries two fiber genes and lineage-specific ORFs at both ends; several deposited ORFs at the ends are not yet declared (section 07).

Genomes were assigned to modules from sequence alone: the genus by best hexon match, and one-fiber versus multi-fiber mastadenoviruses by a census of intact fiber genes classed by literature orthology (Podgorski 2023, PMID 36610683). Deposited names were never used to assign a genome.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Membership by homology to curated seed collections; the deposited name is recorded but never decides.

rows: 2,567 unique proteins assigned (≥80% coverage both ways, best feature ≥1.2× the runner-up)
979 no hit, 59 ambiguous, 408 low coverage, 1 submitter-marked partial

blocks.html: Paralogue families were split into orthogroup features by genome position, and each is called by sequence, never by location. Features with no literature function are named “Uncharacterized lineage-specific protein”. Splice junctions come from the literature and were extended to other lineages by aligning donor and acceptor sites; every spliced product was translated and checked in frame.
Self-recall (each feature’s profiles searched against its own collection) is 100% for nearly every feature; the registry page lists every feature.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: Genome quality from the GTO pipeline on the 916-genome subset, with the essential genes set by the curator’s rules.

blocks.html: Essential genes (copy_num) follow the curator’s rules: never on uncharacterized proteins, special features or lineage-specific genes, and excluded wherever a cutoff, copy-number or coverage problem is on record. Essential here: DBP, HEXON, IVA2, K100, K22, K52, ORF22, PENTON, PIIIA, POL, PROTEASE, PTP, PVI, PVIII, UXP, VIII_N, VI_MAT.

The subset deliberately over-samples unusual genomes, so its quality rate is a floor for the module, not an estimate of it. Poor genomes are dominated by sequence problems: deposits with no cytosine, N gaps, partial genomes and genes interrupted by stop codons.

blocks.html: Unbound deposits are mostly “hypothetical protein” and deposits whose sequence was ambiguous between two features; several name proteins the module does call (for example 22K and E4 ORF1 in the one-fiber mastadenoviruses), so the unbound count is not a count of missed proteins.
